title: Containment lane policy enforcer for tenant-level EU residency and allow/deny semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a 'containment lane' policy enforcer that ensures tenant traffic bound by EU-only residency rules is routed only to certified EU deployment lanes and that tenant-level allowlists/denylists are enforced before any fallback logic runs. The enforcer sits in the request routing path as a PDP (Policy Decision Point) consult and produces an explicit route decision with reason codes suitable for audit logs and Console UI. This ticket covers design, schema, runtime hook, telemetry, and basic rollout (canary + customer opt-in).
acceptance_criteria: Requests with tenant.residency == 'EU_ONLY' must be refused to non-EU lanes by default and logged with reason_code 'residency_violation'

Tenant allowlist entries (tenant.allowlist.lanes) are honored and can enable specific non-EU fallback lanes only when an explicit emergency flag is set on the tenant and the request contains an escape_token
Denylist entries (tenant.denylist.models) block model variants globally for the tenant and are enforced before batching and kernel selection
Route decisions include metadata: lane_id, lane_region, model_variant, reason_code, policy_version and are persisted to the request audit store for 90 days
Console shows per-tenant policy snapshot and recent route denials with links to audit traces
Unit + integration tests cover policy evaluation, allow/deny precedence, emergency passthrough, and rollback behaviour
implementation_notes: High-level flow: 1) Router receives request + tenant headers. 2) Router calls PDP /policy/evaluate with context {tenant_id, residency, request_region_hint, model_family, tier}. 3) PDP evaluates containment_lane rules stored in Policy DB (key: containment_lane:v{version}). 4) PDP returns decision: ALLOW->lane, DENY->reject, FALLBACK->alternative_lane (if allowed). 5) Router applies decision, attaches audit metadata, and proceeds to runtime selection. Policy semantics: - Default: residency constraint takes precedence over cost-tier routing. - Allowlist: explicit tenant allowlists can enable an escape path but require 'escape_token' with limited TTL and must be minted by account ops (logged) - Denylist: blocklist entries short-circuit and mark request as DENIED with model_blocked reason. Data flows: policy evaluation occurs synchronously with <20ms P90 budget; cache decisions for 30s keyed by (tenant, model_family, residency, tier) with immediate invalidation on policy update.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit tests + policy DB schema migration on staging (1 week)
Phase 2: Canary (5% traffic) for internal tenants with residency flags set; monitor routing correctness and latency (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Opt-in for first 10 customers with EU-only contracts, enable console snapshot and audits (1 week)
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% for all EU-only tenants; enable denylist enforcement cluster-wide
Rollback: Toggle feature-flag at Router PDP client to bypass containment policy and fall back to pre-existing routing behavior
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: >0.5% of EU_ONLY requests routed outside EU lanes -> sev2 (policy breach)
Dashboard: per-tenant denied request rate, top reason_codes, and recent policy_version changes
Trace: attach policy_evaluation_id to distributed trace; sample 1% of allowed and denied decisions for deeper inspection
migration_steps: Add containment_lane table to Policy DB with versioning and a migration script (idempotent)
Backfill: No backfill required; new policy defaults to permissive only for non-EU tenants
Deploy PDP + Router client with feature flag turned off, run integration smoke tests
Enable feature flag in staging and verify audits and console snapshots
Coordinate customer ops to mint escape_tokens for any approved emergency allowlists
